qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) for professional services issued by the Delaware Division of Public Health, including procurement schedule, submission deadlines, scope of services, eligibility requirements, and evaluation criteria.

quotes.quote:
REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES 
Delaware Health Fund – FY 2028 Health Programs and Services

Deadline for Receipt of Proposals 
Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT

This Request for Proposals is issued pursuant to that authority and solicits proposals for programs and services to be funded from the Delaware Health Fund in Fiscal Year 2028 (July 1, 2027 – June 30, 2028).
Eligibility: This RFP is open to private organizations.
The following criteria shall be used by the Evaluation Team to evaluate proposals:

findings.title: Business references required
findings.fact: Vendors must provide at least three business references of similar scope and value using Attachment 6.

quotes.quote: Provide at least three (3) business references consisting of current or previous customers of similar scope and value using Attachment 6.

findings.title: No minimum financial turnover requirement specified
findings.fact: The RFP does not specify a minimum financial turnover requirement for vendors.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES

findings.title: Similar work experience is evaluated but not a minimum requirement
findings.fact: Organizational capacity and past performance, including experience operating programs of similar scope, is an evaluation criterion but not a mandatory pre-qualification.

quotes.quote: Organizational Capacity & Past Performance (§ II.E)-governance, financial management, audit history, and experience operating programs of similar scope.

findings.title: Similar work experience required in transmittal letter
findings.fact: The transmittal letter must include the applicant's experience, if any, providing similar services.

quotes.quote: Transmittal Letter as specified on page two (2) of the Request for Proposal including an Applicant's experience, if any, providing similar services.

findings.title: Joint venture / Consortium rules not explicitly stated
findings.fact: The RFP does not explicitly address joint ventures or consortiums, but subcontracting is allowed with prior approval and must be identified in Attachment 7.

quotes.quote: Subcontractors, if any, shall be clearly identified in the Vendor’s proposal by completing Attachment 7, and are subject the approval and acceptance of Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS) Division of Public Health.

None of the equipment and/or services covered by this contract shall be subcontracted without the prior written approval of the State. Only those subcontractors identified in Attachment 7 are considered approved upon award. Changes to those subcontractor(s) listed in Attachment 7 must be approved in writing by the State.

findings.title: Pre-Bid Meeting Not Scheduled
findings.fact: No pre-bid meeting has been scheduled for this RFP.

quotes.quote: Pre-Bid Meeting - Mandatory/Non-Mandatory NONE
A pre-bid meeting has NOT been scheduled for this Request for Proposal.

findings.title: Financial scoring formula
findings.fact: The RFP does not provide a specific financial scoring formula; it states that the contract will be awarded to the most advantageous proposal, not necessarily the lowest price or highest score.

quotes.quote: It should be explicitly noted that the State of Delaware is not obligated to award the contract to the vendor who submits the lowest bid or the vendor who receives the highest total point score, rather the contract will be awarded to the vendor whose proposal is the most advantageous to the State of Delaware.

findings.title: QCBS weightages
findings.fact: The RFP does not specify QCBS (Quality-Cost Based Selection) weightages; it uses a point-based technical evaluation with no explicit cost weight.

quotes.quote: The Proposal Evaluation Team shall assign up to the maximum number of points for each Evaluation Item to each of the proposing vendor’s proposals.

findings.title: Minimum qualifying technical threshold/marks
findings.fact: The RFP does not specify a minimum qualifying technical threshold or marks; it states that proposals must meet all instructions to be considered responsive.

quotes.quote: Therefore, all instructions contained in this RFP shall be met in order to qualify as a responsive and responsible contractor and participate in the Proposal Evaluation Team’s consideration for award.

findings.title: No Bid Bond or Performance Bond Requirement
findings.fact: There is no bid bond requirement and no performance bond requirement.

quotes.quote: There is no Bid Bond Requirement.
There is no Performance Bond requirement.

findings.title: Subscription License Costs and Utilization
findings.fact: Subscription license costs are incurred only when utilized within a fully functioning solution; no costs during implementation. Additional subscription license requests above actual utilization may not exceed 5% of total and are subject to review.

quotes.quote: As a Service subscription license costs shall be incurred at the individual license level only as the individual license is utilized within a fully functioning solution. Subscription costs will not be applicable during periods of implementation and solution development prior to the State’s full acceptance of a working solution. Additional subscription license requests above actual utilization may not exceed 5% of the total and are subject to Delaware budget and technical review.

findings.title: Taxes, Duties, and Fee Structures
findings.fact: The vendor is responsible for all costs of permits and relevant costs. The vendor must comply with state licensing requirements. No specific tax or duty provisions are detailed.

quotes.quote: The cost of permits and other relevant costs required in the performance of the contract shall be borne by the successful vendor.
The vendor shall be properly licensed and authorized to transact business in the State of Delaware as provided in 30 Del. C. § 2101.

findings.title: Invoice Processing Timeline
findings.fact: The State will process payment for each correct invoice within thirty (30) days after receipt.

quotes.quote: The agencies will authorize and process for payment of each invoice within thirty (30) days after the date of receipt of a correct invoice.

findings.title: Liquidated Damages Provision
findings.fact: The State may include liquidated damages provisions for non-performance in the final contract.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware may include in the final contract liquidated damages provisions for non-performance.

findings.title: Taxes Included in Proposal Costs
findings.fact: Proposal costs must include full compensation for all taxes the selected vendor is required to pay.

quotes.quote: The proposal costs shall include full compensation for all taxes that the selected vendor is required to pay.

findings.title: No Additional Fees for P-Card
findings.fact: Vendors shall not charge additional fees for acceptance of P-Card payment and must incorporate costs into proposals.

quotes.quote: Vendors shall not charge additional fees for acceptance of this payment method and shall incorporate any costs into their proposals.

findings.title: Eligibility limited to private organizations
findings.fact: This RFP is open to private organizations only; state-operated programs are not eligible to respond.
findings.business_implication: Only private organizations can bid; state-operated programs are excluded and must use a separate internal process.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that your organization is a private entity and not state-operated. If you are state-operated, do not submit a proposal; instead, follow the separate internal process for state-operated programs.

quotes.quote: Eligibility:  This RFP is open to private organizations.  State-operated programs do not respond to this RFP; funding for state-operated programs is designated by the Department through a separate internal process pursuant to 16 Del. C. § 137(i)(1).

findings.title: Debarment and suspension ineligibility
findings.fact: Any entity currently debarred or suspended is ineligible to bid.
findings.business_implication: If your organization or any subcontractor is currently debarred or suspended, you cannot bid; this is a hard disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Check the System for Award Management (SAM) and any state-level debarment lists to ensure your organization and all proposed subcontractors are not debarred or suspended. If any are, consider not bidding or replacing those subcontractors.

quotes.quote: Any individual, business, organization, corporation, consortium, partnership, joint venture, or any other entity including subcontractors currently debarred or suspended is ineligible to bid.

findings.title: Ineligibility for entities not authorized to conduct business in Delaware
findings.fact: Any entity ineligible to conduct business in the State of Delaware for any reason is ineligible to respond to the RFP.
findings.business_implication: Your organization must be authorized to do business in Delaware; otherwise, you cannot bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your organization is registered and in good standing with the Delaware Division of Corporations. If not, initiate the registration process immediately, as it may take time.

quotes.quote: Any entity ineligible to conduct business in the State of Delaware for any reason is ineligible to respond to the RFP.

findings.title: Exclusions for criminal convictions and ethical violations
findings.fact: The Proposal Evaluation Team may refuse to consider proposals from vendors with certain criminal convictions or ethical violations.
findings.business_implication: Your organization may be disqualified if it or its principals have certain criminal convictions or ethical violations, even if not formally debarred.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct an internal review of any criminal convictions or ethical violations involving your organization or key personnel. If any exist, assess the risk and consider whether to bid or disclose proactively. Legal counsel may be needed.

quotes.quote: The Proposal Evaluation Team reserves the right to refuse to consider any proposal from a vendor who: a. Has been convicted for commission of a criminal offense as an incident to obtaining or attempting to obtain a public or private contract or subcontract, or in the performance of the contract or subcontract: b. Has been convicted under State or Federal statutes of embezzlement, theft, forgery, bribery, falsification or destruction of records, receiving stolen property, or other offense indicating a lack of business integrity or business honesty that currently and seriously affects responsibility as a State contractor: c. Has been convicted or has had a civil judgment entered for a violation under State or Federal antitrust statutes: d. Has violated contract provisions such as: 1) Known failure without good cause to perform in accordance with the specifications or within the time limit provided in the contract; or 2) Failure to perform or unsatisfactory performance in accordance with terms of one or more contracts; e. Has violated ethical standards set out in law or regulation; and f. Any other cause listed in regulations of the State of Delaware determined to be serious and compelling as to affect responsibility as a State contractor, including suspension or debarment by another governmental entity for a cause listed in the regulations.

findings.title: Minimum requirements include Delaware licensure and certifications
findings.fact: Vendors must provide Delaware license(s) and/or certification(s) necessary to perform services as identified in the scope of work.
findings.business_implication: Your organization must hold all required Delaware licenses and certifications to perform the services; failure to provide them will make your proposal non-responsive.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the scope of work to identify all required licenses and certifications. Ensure your organization holds them or can obtain them before award. Include copies in your proposal.

quotes.quote: 1. Provide Delaware license(s) and/or certification(s) necessary to perform services as identified in the scope of work.

findings.title: Proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure required before award
findings.fact: Prior to execution of an award document, the successful Vendor must furnish proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the application process.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure it has or can obtain the necessary Delaware business license before contract execution, otherwise it may be disqualified or delay the award.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify current Delaware business licensure status and initiate application immediately if not already licensed. Include proof or application initiation plan in the proposal.

quotes.quote: Prior to the execution of an award document, the successful Vendor shall either furnish the Agency with proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the process of application where required.

findings.title: Joint venture requires prime contractor designation
findings.fact: Multi-vendor solutions (joint ventures) are allowed only if one partner is designated as the prime contractor, who is responsible for all project management, legal, and financial obligations.
findings.business_implication: If bidding as a joint venture, the consortium must clearly designate a single prime contractor to be the sole point of contact and assume full responsibility, which may affect internal governance and risk allocation.
findings.action_recommendation: If considering a joint venture, designate a prime contractor and clearly define roles and responsibilities in the joint venture agreement. Ensure the prime contractor is prepared to take on all contractual liabilities.

quotes.quote: Multi-vendor solutions (joint ventures) will be allowed only if one of the venture partners is designated as the “prime contractor”. The “prime contractor” must be the joint venture’s contact point for the State of Delaware and be responsible for the joint venture’s performance under the contract, including all project management, legal and financial responsibility for the implementation of all vendor systems.

findings.title: Joint venture agreement must be submitted with proposal
findings.fact: If a joint venture is proposed, a copy of the joint venture agreement clearly describing the responsibilities of the partners must be submitted with the proposal.
findings.business_implication: The joint venture agreement is a mandatory submission; failure to provide it may render the proposal non-responsive.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare and include a comprehensive joint venture agreement with the proposal, detailing each partner's responsibilities, to ensure compliance and avoid disqualification.

quotes.quote: If a joint venture is proposed, a copy of the joint venture agreement clearly describing the responsibilities of the partners must be submitted with the proposal.

findings.title: Equal teaming arrangements not accepted
findings.fact: The State will not accept proposals that reflect an equal teaming arrangement or from vendors who are co-bidding on this RFP.
findings.business_implication: Proposals with equal partnerships or co-bidding arrangements will be rejected, so the bidder must structure any collaboration with a clear prime-subcontractor hierarchy.
findings.action_recommendation: Avoid equal teaming structures. If partnering, ensure one entity is clearly the prime and the other(s) are subcontractors, and reflect this in the proposal.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware will not accept any proposals that reflect an equal teaming arrangement or from vendors who are co-bidding on this RFP.

findings.title: Primary vendor may not participate in more than one proposal
findings.fact: A primary vendor may not participate in more than one proposal in any form.
findings.business_implication: The bidder cannot be the prime in multiple proposals, which may limit its ability to partner with multiple teams; it must choose one proposal to lead.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that the bidder is not listed as a primary vendor in any other proposal for this RFP. If so, decide which proposal to lead and withdraw from others.

quotes.quote: A primary vendor may not participate in more than one proposal in any form.

findings.title: Subcontractors must be approved and identified
findings.fact: Proposed subcontractors must be approved by the Division of Public Health and identified in the proposal by name, services, and qualifications.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must disclose any subcontractors upfront and obtain approval, which may affect teaming arrangements and require additional documentation.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify all subcontractors in the proposal with detailed information and ensure they meet the same requirements as the prime contractor.

quotes.quote: The proposed subcontractors must be approved by the Division of Public Health. Proposed subcontractors must be identified in the proposal; any subcontractor engaged after award must be approved in advance by the Division.

findings.title: Final Bid Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Missing the deadline will result in automatic disqualification, so the bidder must ensure timely submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to submit well before the deadline to avoid last-minute technical issues; confirm the exact time zone and submission portal.

quotes.quote: Deadline for Receipt of Proposals  Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT
All proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.

findings.title: Q&A / Clarification Deadline
findings.fact: Questions must be submitted no later than August 28, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST via the Euna Procurement portal.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must submit any clarifying questions by this deadline to ensure they are addressed before proposal submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly and submit all questions via the portal before the deadline; monitor posted responses.

quotes.quote: Deadline for Questions Date: August 28, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST
Questions may be submitted no later than August 28, 2026 @ 3:00 PM EST.

findings.title: Bid Validity Period
findings.fact: Prices quoted in the proposal shall remain fixed and binding at least through June 30, 2028.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must commit to pricing for a long period, which may expose them to cost increases; they should account for inflation and contingencies.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure pricing is realistic and includes provisions for potential cost escalations; consider the long-term commitment before bidding.

quotes.quote: Prices quoted in the proposal shall remain fixed and binding on the bidder at least through June 30, 2028.

findings.title: Formatting and Envelope Rules
findings.fact: Proposals must be submitted electronically via Euna Procurement; hard copy, mail, facsimile, or email submissions are not accepted.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must use the specified electronic portal and ensure all documents are uploaded correctly; failure to do so will result in rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Familiarize with the Euna Procurement portal, test submission early, and ensure all required documents are uploaded before the deadline.

quotes.quote: Responses submitted by hard copy, mail, facsimile, or e-mail will not be accepted.
To be considered, all proposals must be submitted in through Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire) at https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/ and respond to the items outlined in this RFP.

findings.title: Portal Upload Instructions
findings.fact: Upload submission at https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/; must click submit button before deadline; email confirmation with unique confirmation number will be sent.
findings.business_implication: Failure to click the submit button after uploading files will result in the proposal not being submitted, even if files are uploaded. The confirmation email is the only proof of successful submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all required files are uploaded well before the deadline, click the submit button, and verify receipt of the confirmation email with a unique confirmation number. Retain this email as proof of submission.

quotes.quote: Upload your submission at: https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/
Users must successfully upload all the file(s) and MUST click the submit button before the proposal due date and time.
Users will receive an email confirmation receipt with a unique confirmation number once the submission has been finalized.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Portal
findings.fact: Proposals shall be submitted online at https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/
findings.business_implication: The only acceptable method of submission is through the specified online portal. Submissions via email, mail, or hand delivery will not be accepted.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to submit the proposal exclusively through the Bonfire portal. Familiarize yourself with the portal's requirements and test the submission process in advance to avoid technical issues.

quotes.quote: Proposals shall be submitted online at https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/

findings.title: General Evaluation Requirements
findings.fact: Proposals are evaluated based on six general evaluation requirements: Statement of Need, Alignment with Health Fund Priorities, Program Design and Feasibility, Measurable Outcomes and Evaluation Plan, Organizational Capacity & Past Performance, and Budget Reasonableness and Sustainability.
findings.business_implication: The proposal must comprehensively address all six evaluation criteria to be competitive. Weakness in any area could lower the overall score and reduce chances of funding.
findings.action_recommendation: Structure the proposal to explicitly address each of the six evaluation requirements. Provide clear, evidence-based responses with measurable outcomes and a realistic budget. Ensure alignment with the Health Fund priorities.

quotes.quote:
B.  General Evaluation Requirements  
1.   Statement of Need (§ II.A of proposal)-Delaware-specific evidence of the health need and the service gap the program fills; for returning organizations, including prior-year results. 
2.   Alignment  with  Health  Fund  Priorities  (§  II.B)-fit  with  the  purposes  in  16  Del.  C.  §  137(d), with the strongest weight for direct ties to tobacco prevention and cessation and to cancer prevention, detection, and treatment. 
3.   Program  Design  and  Feasibility  (§  II.C)-goals,  activities,  timeline,  staffing,  and  geographic reach that are specific, coherent, and achievable within the contract year. 
4.   Measurable Outcomes and Evaluation Plan (§ II.D)-specific, verifiable objectives with indicators,  targets,  and  data  sources,  suitable  for  incorporation  into  the  award  agreement. 
5.   Organizational   Capacity   &   Past   Performance   (§   II.E)-governance,   financial   management, audit history, and experience operating programs of similar scope. 
6.   Budget  Reasonableness  and  Sustainability  (§  II.F)=  justified  costs  proportionate  to  reach,  documented  other  funding,  and  a  realistic  plan  given  declining  Master  Settlement Agreement revenue.

findings.title: Funding Priority for Tobacco and Cancer Programs
findings.fact: Proposals with direct ties to tobacco prevention and cessation and to cancer prevention, detection, and treatment receive funding priority.
findings.business_implication: Proposals that directly address tobacco or cancer will have a competitive advantage in the evaluation process. Proposals in other areas may still be funded but are less likely to receive priority.
findings.action_recommendation: If the program has any direct connection to tobacco or cancer, emphasize this in the proposal. If not, consider how to align the program with these priorities or highlight other statutory purposes to remain competitive.

quotes.quote: Accordingly, proposals with direct ties to tobacco prevention and cessation and to cancer prevention, detection, and treatment receive funding priority, and the Division balances awards across funding categories to satisfy this directive.

findings.title: Contract Term and Funding Contingency
findings.fact: The contract term is one year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation. Funding in subsequent fiscal years is not a renewal right.
findings.business_implication: The contract is for one year only and is subject to annual appropriation. There is no guarantee of continued funding beyond the initial term, and future funding requires a new RFP process.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a one-year project scope and budget. Be prepared to reapply in subsequent years if seeking continued funding. Ensure the program can be effectively implemented within a single year and that sustainability plans are realistic given the uncertainty of future funding.

quotes.quote: Contract term is one (1) year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation. Funding in subsequent fiscal years is not a renewal right: continued funding is subject to the annual statutory process under 16 Del. C. § 137(i), including the annual request for proposals, and to annual appropriation.

findings.title: Payment Terms: No Advance Payment, Purchase Order Required
findings.fact: No vendor is to begin any service prior to receipt of a State of Delaware purchase order signed by two authorized representatives. Payments are subject to appropriation and other payment terms.
findings.business_implication: The vendor cannot start work until a formal purchase order is received, which may delay project initiation. Additionally, payments are contingent on state appropriation, introducing financial risk if funds are not allocated.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan project timelines to account for the purchase order lead time. Ensure internal processes are aligned to begin work only after PO receipt. Assess the risk of delayed or non-payment due to appropriation and consider including contingency clauses in subcontracts.

quotes.quote: No vendor is to begin any service prior to receipt of a State of Delaware purchase order signed by two authorized representatives of the agency requesting service, properly processed through the State of Delaware Accounting Office and the Department of Finance.
Payments are subject to appropriation and other payment terms.

findings.title: Payment Milestones and Holdback
findings.fact: The State requires a payment schedule based on defined and measurable milestones, with no advance payments and possible holdback of up to 25% until acceptable performance.
findings.business_implication: Cash flow will be tied to milestone achievements, and up to 25% of contract value may be withheld until the State is satisfied with performance. This could strain the vendor's working capital and increase financial risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a detailed milestone plan with clear, measurable deliverables to ensure timely payments. Budget for potential holdback and consider negotiating the holdback percentage or release criteria. Maintain robust documentation of performance to expedite release of held funds.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware will require a payment schedule based on defined and measurable milestones. Payments for services will not be made in advance of work performed. The State of Delaware may require holdback of contract monies until acceptable performance is demonstrated (as much as 25%).

findings.title: Warranty Period
findings.fact: Vendor must provide a warranty that deliverables function as designed for at least one year from system acceptance, with corrections at Vendor's expense.
findings.business_implication: The vendor is obligated to fix any defects or non-conformities during the one-year warranty period at no additional cost to the State. This could lead to significant post-acceptance costs if the system has issues.
findings.action_recommendation: Allocate sufficient resources and budget for warranty support. Conduct thorough testing before acceptance to minimize defects. Clearly define 'system acceptance' criteria and ensure they are met to start the warranty period. Consider setting aside a contingency fund for potential warranty work.

quotes.quote: The Vendor will provide a warranty that the deliverables provided pursuant to the contract will function as designed for a period of no less than one (1) year from the date of system acceptance. The warranty shall require the Vendor to correct, at its own expense, the setup, configuration, customizations or modifications so that it functions according to the State’s requirements.

findings.title: Prime vendor solely responsible for contract performance
findings.fact: The prime vendor is solely responsible for fulfillment of any contract with the State as a result of this procurement, and assumes all responsibility for work quality, delivery, installation, maintenance, and any supporting services required by a subcontractor.
findings.business_implication: The prime vendor bears full liability for the entire contract, including any failures by subcontractors. This increases the risk of financial and reputational damage if subcontractors underperform.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully select and manage subcontractors, ensuring they have adequate insurance and contractual obligations to the prime vendor. Implement strong oversight and quality control processes. Consider requiring performance bonds or guarantees from subcontractors to mitigate risk.

quotes.quote: The vendor selected shall be solely responsible for contractual performance and management of all subcontract relationships. This contract allows subcontracting assignments; however, vendors assume all responsibility for work quality, delivery, installation, maintenance, and any supporting services required by a subcontractor.
The prime vendor shall be wholly responsible for the entire contract performance whether or not subcontractors are used.

findings.title: Indemnification for temporary staff employment determination
findings.fact: Vendor agrees to hold harmless, indemnify, and defend the State to the maximum extent of any liability arising out of determinations that the State is a dual employer or sole employer of temporary staff.
findings.business_implication: If a government entity determines that the State is a co-employer or sole employer of temporary staff, the vendor must indemnify the State for any resulting liabilities, which could be substantial, including tax and benefit obligations.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that temporary staff are properly classified as employees of the vendor and that all employment taxes and benefits are paid. Review the indemnification clause with legal counsel to understand the full scope of liability. Consider obtaining insurance coverage for employment practices liability.

quotes.quote: In the event that the Internal Revenue Service, or any other third party governmental entity determines that the State of Delaware is a dual employer or the sole employer of any individual temporary staff person(s) provided to the State of Delaware pursuant to this Solicitation, Vendor agrees to hold harmless, indemnify, and defend the State to the maximum extent of any liability to the State arising out of such determinations.

findings.title: General indemnification for vendor's performance
findings.fact: Vendor agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the State of Delaware from any and all liability, suits, actions, or claims arising out of vendor's performance of work or services in connection with the contract.
findings.business_implication: The vendor assumes broad liability for any claims or damages arising from its performance, potentially including those caused by the State's own negligence or third-party actions, leading to significant financial exposure.
findings.action_recommendation: Review and negotiate the scope of the indemnification clause to limit it to claims caused by the vendor's negligence or willful misconduct, and ensure adequate insurance coverage to mitigate potential losses.

quotes.quote: By submitting a proposal, the proposing vendor agrees that in the event it is awarded a contract, it will indemnify and otherwise hold harmless the State of Delaware, its agents and employees from any and all liability, suits, actions, or claims, together with all costs, expenses for attorney’s fees, arising out of the vendor’s, its agents and employees’ performance work or services in connection with the contract.

findings.title: Proprietary rights indemnification
findings.fact: Vendor shall indemnify the State against any loss, cost, damage, expense or liability arising out of third-party claims of infringement of patent, copyright, trade secret or other proprietary rights.
findings.business_implication: The vendor is fully responsible for defending and indemnifying the State against any IP infringement claims, even if the claim is unsuccessful, leading to potentially high legal costs and damages.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct thorough IP due diligence on all proposed products and services, ensure all necessary licenses are obtained, and consider negotiating limitations on the indemnification obligation, such as excluding claims arising from the State's modifications or misuse.

quotes.quote: In the event of any claim, suit or action by any third party against the State of Delaware, the State of Delaware shall promptly notify the vendor in writing and vendor shall defend such claim, suit or action at vendor’s expense, and vendor shall indemnify the State of Delaware against any loss, cost, damage, expense or liability arising out of such claim, suit or action (including, without limitation, litigation costs, lost employee time, and counsel fees) whether or not such claim, suit or action is successful.

findings.title: Vendor liable for all losses, penalties, damages
findings.fact: Vendor is liable for any and all losses, penalties, damages, expenses, attorney's fees, judgments, and/or settlements incurred by reason of injury to persons or property arising out of vendor's negligent performance under the contract.
findings.business_implication: The vendor bears full financial responsibility for any negligent acts or omissions, including consequential damages, which could be substantial and potentially exceed insurance coverage.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure robust risk management practices and adequate insurance coverage, including professional liability and general liability, to cover potential claims. Consider negotiating a cap on liability or mutual indemnification provisions.

quotes.quote: Vendor recognizes that it is operating as an independent contractor and that it is liable for any and all losses, penalties, damages, expenses, attorney’s fees, judgments, and/or settlements incurred by reason of injury to or death of any and all persons, or injury to any and all property, of any nature, arising out of the vendor’s negligent performance under this contract, and particularly without limiting the foregoing, caused by, resulting from, or arising out of any act of omission on the part of the vendor in their negligent performance under this contract.

findings.title: Insurance requirements for workers' compensation and employer's liability
findings.fact: Vendor must maintain workers' compensation and employer's liability insurance in accordance with applicable law.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must secure and maintain statutory workers' compensation and employer's liability insurance, which is a mandatory cost of doing business and protects against employee injury claims.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that the vendor's current insurance policies meet the state's requirements and are maintained throughout the contract term. Provide proof of insurance to the State as required.

quotes.quote: The vendor shall maintain such insurance as will protect against claims under Worker’s Compensation Act and from any other claims for damages for personal injury, including death, which may arise from operations under this contract.
Worker’s Compensation and Employer’s Liability Insurance in accordance with applicable law.

findings.title: Commercial general liability insurance minimum limits
findings.fact: Vendor must carry Commercial General Liability insurance with limits of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 per aggregate.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must obtain and maintain CGL insurance with specified minimum limits, which is a significant cost and a prerequisite for contract award.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the vendor's CGL policy meets or exceeds the required limits and is maintained for the entire contract duration. Obtain certificates of insurance and review policy terms to confirm coverage.

quotes.quote: Commercial General Liability - $1,000,000 per occurrence/$3,000,000 per aggregate.

findings.title: Automotive liability insurance requirements
findings.fact: Vendor must maintain automotive liability insurance covering all automotive units used in the work, with specified minimum limits including $1,000,000 combined single limit each accident for bodily injury, $250,000 for property damage, and uninsured/underinsured motorists coverage.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must secure and maintain specific automotive liability insurance with high limits, which could increase insurance costs. Failure to comply may lead to contract non-compliance or termination.
findings.action_recommendation: Review current automotive insurance policies to ensure they meet or exceed the specified limits. Obtain and submit a Certificate of Insurance (COI) to the State before commencing work. Consider obtaining higher limits if cost-effective.

quotes.quote: Automotive Liability Insurance covering all automotive units used in the work (including all units leased from and/or provided by the State to Vendor pursuant to this Agreement as well as all units used by Vendor, regardless of the identity of the registered owner, used by Vendor for completing the Work required by this Agreement to include but not limited to transporting Delaware clients or staff), providing coverage on a primary non-contributory basis with limits of not less than: (a) $1,000,000 combined single limit each accident, for bodily injury; (b) $250,000 for property damage to others; (c) $25,000 per person per accident Uninsured/Underinsured Motorists coverage; (d) $25,000 per person, $300,000 per accident Personal Injury Protection (PIP) benefits as provided for in 21 Del. C. §2118; and (e) Comprehensive coverage for all leased vehicles, which shall cover the replacement cost of the vehicle in the event of collision, damage or other loss.

findings.title: Professional liability insurance options
findings.fact: Vendor must carry at least one of the following depending on scope: Medical/Professional Liability, Miscellaneous Errors and Omissions, or Product Liability, each with $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must obtain appropriate professional liability insurance based on the services provided, which may add significant cost. Inadequate coverage could expose the vendor to financial risk in case of claims.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the scope of work to determine which type of professional liability insurance is required. Obtain and maintain the necessary policy with at least $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate. Provide COI as proof.

quotes.quote: The successful vendor must carry at least one of the following depending on the scope of work being performed. (1) Medical/Professional Liability - $1,000,000 per occurrence/$3,000,000 per aggregate (2) Miscellaneous Errors and Omissions - $1,000,000 per occurrence/ $3,000,000 per aggregate (3) Product Liability - $1,000,000 per occurrence/$3,000,000 aggregate

findings.title: No additional insured for State
findings.fact: The State of Delaware shall not be named as an additional insured on any policy required under the agreement.
findings.business_implication: The vendor cannot rely on the State's insurance coverage; the vendor's own insurance must cover claims. This may increase the vendor's liability exposure.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the vendor's insurance policies are adequate to cover potential claims without the State as an additional insured. Consider purchasing higher limits or additional coverage if necessary.

quotes.quote: In no event shall the State of Delaware be named as an additional insured on any policy required under this agreement.
The State of Delaware shall not be named as an additional insured.

findings.title: State self-insurance not applicable if vendor complies
findings.fact: If vendor has complied with insurance terms, the State's self-insured program shall not provide any coverage for any loss.
findings.business_implication: The vendor cannot expect the State's self-insurance to cover any losses if the vendor has met its insurance obligations. This reinforces the vendor's responsibility to maintain adequate coverage.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that all required insurance policies are in place and maintained throughout the contract period. Do not rely on the State's self-insurance for any coverage.

quotes.quote: To the extent that Vendor has complied with the terms of this Agreement and has procured insurance coverage for all vehicles Leased and/or operated by Vendor as part of this Agreement, the State of Delaware’s self-insured insurance program shall not provide any coverage whether coverage is sought as primary, co-primary, excess or umbrella insurer or coverage for any loss of any nature.

findings.title: Liability for failure to accurately estimate costs
findings.fact: The State shall bear no responsibility or increase obligation for a vendor's failure to accurately estimate the costs or resources required to meet the obligations defined in the proposal.
findings.business_implication: The vendor bears the risk of cost overruns or underestimation. The State will not compensate for additional costs due to inaccurate estimates, potentially impacting profitability.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct thorough cost estimation, including contingency for inflation and unforeseen expenses. Ensure pricing is realistic and covers all potential costs. Avoid underbidding to win the contract.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware shall bear no responsibility or increase obligation for a vendor’s failure to accurately estimate the costs or resources required to meet the obligations defined in the proposal.

findings.title: Liability for confidential information disclosure
findings.fact: Vendor assumes the risk that confidential business information included in a proposal may enter the public domain.
findings.business_implication: The State may disclose confidential information if it determines it is not exempt under FOIA, and the vendor cannot hold the State liable for such disclosure. This could expose trade secrets or proprietary information.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the confidentiality procedure and only mark truly confidential information. Consider limiting the amount of confidential information in the proposal and use separate files as instructed. Consult legal counsel on the designation process.

quotes.quote: Accordingly, vendor(s) assume the risk that confidential business information included in a proposal may enter the public domain.

findings.title: Liability for breach of no-lobbying warranty
findings.fact: For breach of warranty regarding lobbying or gratuities, the State may annul the contract without liability or deduct/recover the full amount of commission, percentage, brokerage, or contingent fee.
findings.business_implication: Any violation of the no-lobbying and gratuities warranty could result in contract termination without compensation and financial penalties, including recovery of any fees paid. This poses a significant financial and reputational risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure strict compliance with all lobbying and gratuity restrictions. Implement internal controls to prevent any unauthorized contact with State employees. Review all agreements with third parties to ensure no contingent fees are involved.

quotes.quote: For breach or violation of this warranty, the State of Delaware shall have the right to annul any contract resulting from this RFP without liability or at its discretion deduct from the contract price or otherwise recover the full amount of such commission, percentage, brokerage or contingent fee.

findings.title: Liability for failure to provide emergency contact
findings.fact: Failure to provide emergency response point of contact could render the proposal as non-responsive.
findings.business_implication: If the required 24/7 emergency contact information is not provided, the proposal may be rejected as non-responsive, leading to disqualification from the procurement process.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the proposal includes the names and 24/7 contact numbers of designated individuals for emergency response. Double-check that this information is complete and accurate before submission.

quotes.quote: Failure to provide this information could render the proposal as non-responsive.

findings.title: Cost of Audit Disallowances Borne by Vendor
findings.fact: The Vendor bears the cost of any contract audit disallowances and must reimburse the State from its own resources.
findings.business_implication: If the State audits the vendor's financial records and disallows certain costs, the vendor must reimburse the State from its own funds, not from contract revenues. This could result in unexpected financial losses.
findings.action_recommendation: Maintain accurate and compliant financial records to minimize audit disallowances. Ensure that all costs charged to the contract are allowable and properly documented. Set aside contingency funds to cover potential disallowances.

quotes.quote: The cost of any Contract audit disallowances resulting from the examination of the Vendor's financial records will be borne by the Vendor. Reimbursement to the State for disallowances shall be drawn from the Vendor's own resources and not charged to Contract cost or cost pools indirectly charging Contract costs.

findings.title: Vendor Responsible for All Products and Services
findings.fact: The successful Vendor is responsible for all products and services required by the RFP, even if subcontracted.
findings.business_implication: The vendor remains fully liable for the performance of all subcontractors. Any failure by a subcontractor to deliver as required will be the vendor's responsibility, potentially leading to penalties or contract termination.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully select and manage subcontractors, ensuring they are capable and reliable. Include clear performance requirements and remedies in subcontracts. Maintain oversight and contingency plans to mitigate subcontractor risks.

quotes.quote: The successful Vendor(s) shall be responsible for all products and services as required by this RFP whether or not the Vendor or its subcontractor provided final fulfillment of the order.

findings.title: Penalties for Background Check Violations
findings.fact: Violation of background check requirements may subject the Vendor to penalty, including contract cancellation for cause.
findings.business_implication: Failure to comply with background check requirements can lead to contract termination, resulting in loss of revenue and potential reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust background check processes for all employees and subcontractors serving the contract, and maintain documentation to demonstrate compliance.

quotes.quote: A violation of this condition represents a violation of the contract terms and conditions, and may subject the Vendor to penalty, including contract cancellation for cause.

findings.title: Criminal and Civil Sanctions for FTI Disclosure
findings.fact: Unauthorized disclosure of FTI can result in criminal fines and imprisonment, and civil damages.
findings.business_implication: Unauthorized disclosure of FTI can lead to severe legal consequences, including criminal penalties and civil damages, which could be financially devastating and harm the company's reputation.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all personnel handling FTI are trained on the strict confidentiality requirements and the severe penalties for unauthorized disclosure. Implement strict access controls and monitoring to prevent any unauthorized access or disclosure.

quotes.quote: Each officer or employee of a contractor to whom FTI is or may be disclosed shall be notified in writing that FTI disclosed to such officer or employee can be used only for a purpose and to the extent authorized herein, and that further disclosure of any FTI for a purpose not authorized herein constitutes a felony punishable upon conviction by a fine of as much as $5,000 or imprisonment for as long as 5 years, or both, together with the costs of prosecution.

Each officer or employee of a contractor to whom FTI is or may be disclosed shall be notified in writing that any such unauthorized access, inspection or disclosure of FTI may also result in an award of civil damages against the officer or employee in an amount equal to the sum of the greater of $1,000 for each unauthorized access, inspection, or disclosure, or the sum of actual damages sustained as a result of such unauthorized access, inspection, or disclosure, plus in the case of a willful unauthorized access, inspection, or disclosure or an unauthorized access/inspection or disclosure which is the result of gross negligence, punitive damages, plus the cost of the action.

findings.title: Vendor Responsible for Subcontractor Compliance
findings.fact: The Vendor must ensure that subcontractors comply with all FTI safeguard requirements and assumes obligations toward subcontractors.
findings.business_implication: The vendor is fully responsible for any subcontractor's failure to comply with FTI safeguards, which could lead to contract termination and legal liabilities.
findings.action_recommendation: Flow down all FTI safeguard requirements to subcontractors in writing, and conduct regular audits to ensure compliance. Include indemnification clauses in subcontracts to protect the vendor.

quotes.quote: To the extent the terms, provisions, duties, requirements, and obligations of this contract apply to performing services with FTI, the contractor shall assume toward the subcontractor all obligations, duties and responsibilities that the agency under this contract assumes toward the contractor, and the subcontractor shall assume toward the contractor all the same obligations, duties and responsibilities which the contractor assumes toward the agency under this contract.

findings.title: Right to Void Contract for FTI Safeguard Failure
findings.fact: The agency has the right to void the contract if the contractor fails to meet FTI safeguard terms.
findings.business_implication: Failure to meet FTI safeguard terms can result in immediate contract voidance, leading to loss of revenue and potential legal action.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement comprehensive FTI safeguard measures, including security controls, employee training, and regular audits, to ensure full compliance and avoid contract voidance.

quotes.quote: The agency will have the right to void the contract if the contractor fails to meet the terms of FTI safeguards described herein.

findings.title: Termination for Cause
findings.fact: The State may terminate the contract for cause if the Vendor fails to fulfill obligations, and the Vendor may be entitled to compensation for satisfactory work completed.
findings.business_implication: Failure to meet contractual obligations can lead to termination, but the vendor may receive compensation for completed work, mitigating some financial loss.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all contractual obligations are met in a timely and proper manner to avoid termination. If termination occurs, document all completed work to claim just compensation.

quotes.quote: If, for any reasons, or through any cause, the Vendor fails to fulfill in timely and proper manner its obligations under this Contract, or if the Vendor violates any of the covenants, agreements, or stipulations of this Contract, the State shall thereupon have the right to terminate this contract by giving written notice to the Vendor of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination. In that event, all finished or unfinished documents, data, studies, surveys, drawings, maps, models, photographs, and reports or other material prepared by the Vendor under this Contract shall, at the option of the State, become its property, and the Vendor shall be entitled to receive just and equitable compensation for any satisfactory work completed on such documents and other materials which is usable to the State.

findings.title: Covenant against Contingent Fees
findings.fact: The Vendor warrants that no contingent fees were paid to secure the contract; breach allows the State to annul the contract or recover the full amount of such fees.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must ensure that no contingent fees have been paid to any third party to secure the contract, as any violation could lead to contract annulment or financial recovery by the State, posing a significant financial and reputational risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct an internal review to confirm that no contingent fees have been paid or promised to any person or agency in connection with this bid. Maintain documentation of any legitimate commissions or fees paid to bona fide employees or established commercial agencies to demonstrate compliance.

quotes.quote: The successful vendor will warrant that no person or selling agency has been employed or retained to solicit or secure this contract upon an agreement of understanding for a commission or percentage, brokerage or contingent fee excepting bona-fide employees, bona-fide established commercial or selling agencies maintained by the Vendor for the purpose of securing business. For breach or violation of this warranty the State of Delaware shall have the right to annul the contract without liability or at its discretion to deduct from the contract price or otherwise recover the full amount of such commission, percentage, brokerage or contingent fee.

findings.title: State's Right to Cancel Solicitation
findings.fact: The State reserves the right to cancel the solicitation at any time during the procurement process, for any reason or for no reason.
findings.business_implication: The State can cancel the solicitation at any time without liability, meaning the vendor may incur bid preparation costs with no guarantee of award or compensation.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the potential costs of bid preparation and consider whether the opportunity justifies the risk of cancellation. Avoid making significant investments or commitments based solely on this solicitation until a contract is executed.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time during the procurement process, for any reason or for no reason.

findings.title: State's Right to Terminate Negotiations
findings.fact: The State may terminate negotiations at any time and for any reason, or for no reason.
findings.business_implication: Even if the vendor is selected for negotiations, the State can walk away without any commitment, leaving the vendor with no contract and potentially wasted time and resources.
findings.action_recommendation: During negotiations, avoid making concessions or incurring costs that cannot be recovered if the State terminates. Keep negotiation strategies flexible and be prepared to walk away if terms become unfavorable.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware may terminate negotiations at any time and for any reason, or for no reason.

findings.title: Termination for Default
findings.fact: Vendors who have violated contract provisions such as known failure without good cause to perform in accordance with specifications or within time limits may be excluded from consideration, indicating potential termination for default.
findings.business_implication: Past performance issues, such as failure to meet contract specifications or deadlines, can lead to exclusion from consideration for this contract, and similar violations during the contract could result in termination for default.
findings.action_recommendation: Review past contract performance to ensure there are no issues that could be considered a violation. If any past performance issues exist, be prepared to explain them and demonstrate corrective actions taken. During contract execution, strictly adhere to all specifications and timelines to avoid default.

quotes.quote: Has violated contract provisions such as: 1) Known failure without good cause to perform in accordance with the specifications or within the time limit provided in the contract; or 2) Failure to perform or unsatisfactory performance in accordance with terms of one or more contracts;

findings.title: No Force Majeure Conditions
findings.fact: The RFP does not contain any force majeure conditions.
findings.business_implication: The absence of force majeure provisions means the vendor may be held liable for non-performance due to unforeseen events beyond its control, such as natural disasters or pandemics, without contractual relief.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the risks of unforeseen events that could impact performance. Consider whether to request the inclusion of a force majeure clause during negotiations, or evaluate if the vendor's insurance and business continuity plans adequately mitigate such risks.

quotes.quote: STATE OF DELAWARE DIVISON OF PUBLIC HEALTH 5 A. Minimum Requirements

findings.title: Termination for Convenience by State
findings.fact: The State of Delaware has the sole right to reject any proposal, award to other than lowest priced proposal, or not to award a contract. The Evaluation Team may terminate negotiations with any or all vendors at its discretion.
findings.business_implication: The State retains broad discretion in the award process, meaning the bidder may not be selected even if it offers the lowest price or highest score. The State can also terminate negotiations at any time, so the bidder should not assume that reaching negotiation stage guarantees a contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare a competitive and compelling proposal that highlights unique value beyond price. Be prepared for the possibility of non-selection and avoid incurring significant costs before contract execution. During negotiations, maintain flexibility and respond promptly to State requests.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware has the sole right to select the successful vendor(s) for award, to reject any proposal as unsatisfactory or non-responsive, to award a contract to other than the lowest priced proposal, to award multiple contracts, or not to award a contract, as a result of this RFP.
The Team may negotiate with one or more vendors during the same period and may, at its discretion, terminate negotiations with any or all vendors.

findings.title: Termination for Cause
findings.fact: The State may terminate the contract for cause if the Vendor fails to fulfill obligations, with at least 20 days written notice. The Vendor has 5 days to respond and propose corrective actions.
findings.business_implication: The State can terminate the contract if the vendor fails to meet obligations, with a relatively short notice period. The vendor has a limited window (5 days) to respond and propose corrective actions, which may be insufficient to address complex issues. Termination for cause could damage the vendor's reputation and lead to financial losses.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure strict compliance with all contractual obligations and maintain robust project management to avoid defaults. Establish internal processes to quickly respond to any notice of default, including preparing a corrective action plan within the 5-day window. Consider negotiating for a longer response period if possible.

quotes.quote: If, for any reasons, or through any cause, the Vendor fails to fulfill in timely and proper manner its obligations under this Contract, or if the Vendor violates any of the covenants, agreements, or stipulations of this Contract, the State shall thereupon have the right to terminate this contract by giving written notice to the Vendor of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination.
On receipt of the contract cancellation notice from the State, the Vendor shall have no less than five (5) days to provide a written response and may identify a method(s) to resolve the violation(s).

findings.title: Termination for Convenience
findings.fact: The State may terminate the contract at any time for convenience with at least 20 days written notice. The Vendor is entitled to compensation for satisfactory work completed and usable to the State.
findings.business_implication: The State can terminate the contract without cause, providing only 20 days' notice. While the vendor will be compensated for satisfactory work completed and usable to the State, this may not cover all costs or lost profits. This introduces uncertainty and potential financial risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for the possibility of early termination by maintaining detailed records of work performed and costs incurred. Ensure that all deliverables are documented and meet State requirements to maximize compensation. Consider negotiating for more favorable termination compensation terms, such as including a termination fee or coverage of non-cancelable commitments.

quotes.quote: The State may terminate this Contract at any time by giving written notice of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination.

In that event, all finished or unfinished documents, data, studies, surveys, drawings, models, photographs, reports, supplies, and other materials shall, at the option of the State, become its property and the Vendor shall be entitled to receive compensation for any satisfactory work completed on such documents and other materials, and which is usable to the State.

findings.title: Notice Periods for Termination
findings.fact: Both termination for cause and termination for convenience require at least 20 days written notice before the effective date of termination.
findings.business_implication: The 20-day notice period is relatively short, giving the vendor limited time to wind down operations or address issues. This could lead to abrupt project cessation and potential financial losses.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop contingency plans for potential termination, including transition procedures and communication strategies. Maintain open lines of communication with the State to receive early warnings of potential termination. Consider negotiating for a longer notice period, especially for complex projects.

quotes.quote: at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination.
at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination.

findings.title: Post-Termination Obligations
findings.fact: Upon termination for cause or convenience, all finished or unfinished documents, data, and other materials prepared by the Vendor become the property of the State at the State's option.
findings.business_implication: The State can take ownership of all work product, including unfinished materials, which may include proprietary information or intellectual property. This could impact the vendor's ability to reuse or protect its work.
findings.action_recommendation: Before contract execution, clarify ownership and intellectual property rights. Ensure that any proprietary information is clearly identified and protected. Consider negotiating limitations on the State's rights to use the materials, especially for unfinished work. Maintain copies of all work product for your own records.

quotes.quote: In that event, all finished or unfinished documents, data, studies, surveys, drawings, maps, models, photographs, and reports or other material prepared by the Vendor under this Contract shall, at the option of the State, become its property

In that event, all finished or unfinished documents, data, studies, surveys, drawings, models, photographs, reports, supplies, and other materials shall, at the option of the State, become its property

findings.title: Payment Obligations upon Termination
findings.fact: Upon termination for cause or convenience, the Vendor is entitled to receive just and equitable compensation for satisfactory work completed that is usable to the State.
findings.business_implication: The vendor may receive compensation for work completed up to termination, but only if the work is deemed satisfactory and usable by the State. This creates uncertainty about the amount recoverable, as the State has discretion in determining what is 'usable'.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure thorough documentation of all deliverables and their usability. Maintain clear records of work progress and acceptance. Consider negotiating more specific payment terms in the contract to clarify compensation upon termination.

quotes.quote: the Vendor shall be entitled to receive just and equitable compensation for any satisfactory work completed on such documents and other materials which is usable to the State.
the Vendor shall be entitled to receive compensation for any satisfactory work completed on such documents and other materials, and which is usable to the State.

findings.title: Contract Term Discrepancy
findings.fact: The contract term is stated as one year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, but the RFP also mentions a Fiscal Year 2029 RFP anticipated release on or before July 1, 2027, which could be ambiguous.
findings.business_implication: There is ambiguity regarding the actual contract duration and the possibility of a follow-on contract. This could affect resource planning and financial projections, as the vendor may need to prepare for a potential continuation or re-compete.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from the State on the intended contract term and the relationship between the initial contract and the Fiscal Year 2029 RFP. Plan for potential re-compete and ensure pricing and resources are flexible.

quotes.quote: Contract term is one (1) year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation.

Organizations funded in Fiscal Year 2028 that seek Fiscal Year 2029 funding must respond to the Fiscal Year 2029 RFP (anticipated release on or before July 1, 2027), which is expected to include a streamlined continuation response for organizations proposing to continue substantially the same program.

findings.title: Order of Precedence Clause
findings.fact: The order of precedence for contract documents is specified, but it may conflict with other sections that state the RFP and vendor's response will be incorporated into the contract.
findings.business_implication: Potential conflicts between the RFP, vendor's response, and the final contract could lead to disputes over which terms prevail. This may affect the vendor's rights and obligations, especially if the vendor's response contains favorable terms that could be overridden.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the order of precedence and ensure that the vendor's response is consistent with the RFP and the final contract. During negotiations, clarify any ambiguities and ensure that key commercial terms are included in the contract itself to avoid being overridden.

quotes.quote: In the event there is any discrepancy between any of these contract documents, the following order of documents governs so that the former prevails over the latter: contract, State of Delaware’s RFP, Vendor’s response to the RFP and purchase order.
This RFP and the selected vendor’s response to this RFP will be incorporated as part of any formal contract.
